panels.title: Timeline read p99, by path
panels.description: The materialised path reads one Redis range; the source path assembles the page from Postgres because Redis was unavailable. Plotted together because the gap between them is the cost of degrading, and a single averaged line would hide it.

panels.title: Reads by path
panels.description: A ratio, not a count. 'The fallback fired 4,000 times' means nothing without knowing whether that was four percent of traffic or all of it.

panels.title: Degraded
panels.description: 1 while the materialised read path is unavailable. A gauge rather than a counter, because the question at 3am is 'is it happening now' and a counter can only answer 'has it ever'.

panels.title: Downstream gRPC calls per GraphQL request
panels.description: The number phases 2 through 5 exist to move: 163 naive, 4 after batching. Plotted as a p99 so one expensive query is visible rather than averaged away.

panels.title: Post cache hit ratio by tier
panels.description: local is the in-process LRU, redis is shared across replicas, source is the only tier that costs a database read. The claim of phase 5 is that source stays flat while readers climb.

panels.title: Fanout duration p99, by follower bucket
panels.description: Bucketed by author size because that is the variable: the same code takes 4ms for a hundred followers and twenty-four seconds for five hundred thousand, which is the whole argument for the phase 4 threshold.

panels.title: JetStream consumer backlog
panels.description: Undelivered plus in-flight, which is what KEDA scales on. Reporting only undelivered made a twenty-four-second fanout read as zero in phase 4 — the instrumentation bug that started the habit of distrusting flattering numbers.

panels.title: Write amplification
panels.description: Follower timelines written per second. The phase 4 cutover took a single 500k-follower post from 500,000 writes to zero.

panels.title: Outbox lag
panels.description: The oldest unpublished event's age. It is the gap between a post being committed and the world being told, and it stays flat unless the bus is gone — during the phase 8 NATS partition it grew for the length of the outage and drained in four seconds.

panels.title: Fanout outcomes
panels.description: Anything but ok is an event that will be redelivered or parked.

panels.title: Live subscription connections
panels.description: Per replica. Phase 6 held 2,000 on one gateway in 140 MiB.

panels.title: Publish-to-client delivery p99
panels.description: From the post's own createdAt to the byte reaching a client's buffer, so the number covers the outbox poll, JetStream, the fanout and the socket rather than only the gateway.

panels.title: Backpressure
panels.description: Dropped is the policy working, not a failure; a rising rate means clients are slower than the timeline is moving. Evicted is a connection closed for falling too far behind.

panels.title: Rate limit decisions
panels.description: The ratio of limited to allowed is what says whether a limit is protecting the service or breaking a legitimate client. failures_total is requests allowed because Redis was unreachable — the limiter fails open, and that counter is where the alert belongs.

panels.title: Gateway request duration p99
panels.description: By GraphQL operation rather than by path, because every request is a POST to /query and the path carries no information at all.
